headline: This law changes how the VA applies the 85/15 Rule, which limits GI Bill enrollment at schools where too many students have their costs paid by the school or the VA.
what_it_does: The 85/15 Rule generally stops the VA from approving a veteran's enrollment at a school where more than 85% of students have tuition or charges paid by the school or the VA. This law adds an exception for payment plans that a school has a history of offering and that are paid off within 180 days after the term ends. It also requires the VA to set up a way for schools to ask for a review when they are found to be over the 85% limit. The law also changes the existing 35% exemption and exempts programs with fewer than 10 students that have costs paid by the school or the VA.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans and eligible GI Bill beneficiaries
who_it_affects.how: Some veterans may be able to use GI Bill benefits at schools that might previously have been blocked under the 85/15 Rule.

who_it_affects.group: Schools that enroll veterans and GI Bill beneficiaries
who_it_affects.how: Schools with certain payment plans or small programs may now fall outside the 85/15 Rule, and schools gain a formal way to request review of VA determinations.
The VA must create a process for schools to request review of 85/15 determinations.
